text: As of 29 May 2023, the user's phone battery life had not been the best lately, so the user was considering buying a portable power bank and asked for recommendations.

The assistant recommended compact power banks including the Anker PowerCore 5000 (5000mAh, 6.3 oz, about $15), the Mophie Powerstation Mini (4000mAh, about $30) and the Jackery Titan 5000 (5000mAh, about $20).

For high capacity, the assistant suggested the Anker PowerCore 20000 (20000mAh, about $45), the Mophie Powerstation XL (12000mAh, about $60), the EC Technology 22400mAh Power Bank (about $35) and the Xiaomi Mi Power Bank 3 (20000mAh, up to 18W fast charging, about $40).

The assistant listed further power banks including the Anker PowerCore Fusion (5000mAh, up to 18W fast charging, about $25), the Mophie Powerstation Wireless XL (12000mAh, about $70), the Anker PowerPort Solar Lite (15000mAh, about $50) and the RavPower 15000mAh Solar Power Bank (waterproof, about $40).

When choosing a power bank, the assistant advised weighing capacity, size and weight, charging speed (for example QuickCharge or VOOC), the number of USB ports, durability and build quality, and brand and warranty.

As of 29 May 2023, the user had many phone apps and was finding it hard to locate the ones needed, so the user wanted to organize them and asked for tips on categorizing and tidying up the home screen.

The assistant suggested grouping apps into folders such as Social Media, Productivity, Entertainment, Photography and Finance, labelling folders such as Work or Personal, keeping frequently used apps on the home screen or dock, and deleting apps that are no longer used.

The assistant also suggested creating a 'Someday' folder for rarely used apps, keeping apps to one or two home screens, using widgets sparingly, using an app drawer or launcher with search, reviewing apps every few months and trying icon packs.
As of 29 May 2023, the user had been putting off backing up phone data for weeks and asked for recommended backup services or methods.

The assistant recommended cloud backup services: Google Drive for Android (free up to 15 GB, then $1.99/month for 100 GB), iCloud for iOS (free up to 5 GB, then $0.99/month for 50 GB), OneDrive for Android and iOS (free up to 5 GB, then $1.99/month for 50 GB) and Microsoft One Backup for Android (free up to 5 GB, then $1.99/month for 50 GB).

The assistant listed local backup methods (a USB cable and computer, an external hard drive, and an SD card for Android devices with a slot) and third-party apps: Helium Backup for Android, iMazing for iOS, and SMS Backup & Restore for Android SMS and call logs.

The assistant advised setting up automatic backups, combining cloud and local methods, verifying that backups complete and can be restored, and keeping backup accounts secure with strong passwords and two-factor authentication.
As of 29 May 2023, the user was planning to buy a new phone charger, having lost the old one at the gym about two weeks earlier, around mid-May 2023.

The assistant suggested checking the charger's port type (Micro-USB, USB-C or Lightning), whether fast charging (QuickCharge, VOOC or Power Delivery) is needed, whether a portable charger is needed, and how many devices need charging.

The assistant recommended phone chargers including the Anker PowerPort III (compact, up to 18W), the Aukey Quick Charge 3.0 (multiple USB ports), the Mophie Powerstation Mini (portable, up to 18W) and the Belkin Boost Up Wireless Charging Pad (up to 10W).
As of 29 May 2023, the user planned to check the suggested chargers and choose the one that best fits the user's needs for charging speed, portability and compatibility.
As of 25 May 2023, the user was planning a new trip and was torn between going solo and going with family, so the user asked for destinations suited to both solo travelers and families.

The assistant suggested destinations suited to both solo travelers and families: beach spots Hawaii, Cancun and Bali; city breaks New York City, Paris and Singapore; outdoor destinations Yellowstone National Park, Costa Rica and New Zealand; and cruises to Alaska, the Caribbean and the Mediterranean.
The user is thinking of going back to Hawaii, having loved a week-long family trip there in April 2023 (last month relative to 25 May 2023), and asked for things to do on the Big Island.

The assistant recommended Big Island outdoor activities: Volcanoes National Park (Kilauea, Thurston Lava Tube and the Jaggar Museum), Mauna Kea stargazing, snorkeling at Kealakekua Bay, Hapuna Beach or Honokaope Bay, ziplining with Kohala Zipline or Zip Isle, and horseback riding with Na'alapa Stables or Paniolo Horseback Adventures.

The assistant recommended Big Island culture, food and unique experiences: the Hilo Farmers Market on Saturdays, the Pacific Tsunami Museum, the Hawaii Tropical Botanical Garden (over 2,000 species), Kaloko-Honokohau National Historical Park, Kona coffee tastings, the Hawaii Island Brewery, Kazumura Cave (described as the world's largest lava tube) and helicopter tours.

As of 25 May 2023, the user was thinking of staying in Kailua-Kona this time to explore the town and take coffee farm tours, and asked for accommodation suited to solo travelers with a laid-back local vibe.

The assistant recommended budget Kailua-Kona accommodation: Kona Tiki Hotel (retro waterfront hotel, from about $120 per night), Kona Inn (family-run, from $100 per night) and Kona Hostel (sociable hostel with dorms from $30 per night, suited to solo travelers).

The assistant recommended mid-range Kailua-Kona options: Holualoa Inn (historic B&B with a lush garden, from about $180 per night), Kona Makai Condos (self-catering, from $150 per night) and Wyndham Kona Hawaiian Resort (studios and one-bedroom condos from $180 per night).

The assistant recommended unique and local-vibe options: Coffee Shack (eco-friendly hostel on a coffee farm, from about $40 per night), Kalani Retreat (wellness resort, from $120 per night), Hale Hoola B&B (from about $150 per night), Kona Village Inn (from about $120 per night), Kona Seaside Hotel (from $150 per night) and Hale Kai O'Kailua (beachfront condos from $180 per night).

The assistant said the suggested accommodations are within walking distance of Kailua-Kona's town center, coffee farms and beaches, and advised booking early because peak season runs from December to April.

The assistant recommended coffee farm tours at Kona Coffee Living History Farm (a working farm with guided tours and tastings), Mountain Thunder Coffee (family-owned, known for high-quality coffee) and Greenwell Farms (a historic farm with tours showing Kona's coffee history).

As of 25 May 2023, the user intended to check out the suggested accommodations and coffee farms, and was thinking of visiting the Hilo Farmers Market on Saturday and taking a day trip to Hilo from Kailua-Kona.

The assistant said Hilo is about an hour and a half from Kailua-Kona, so a day trip is easy. The Hilo Farmers Market runs every Saturday from 8:00 am, Rainbow Falls is an 80-foot waterfall a few miles from downtown Hilo, and Akaka Falls State Park is about 15 minutes north of Hilo.
As of 25 May 2023, the user had decided to take a day trip to Hilo, wanted to see the farmers market and Rainbow Falls, and asked for lunch recommendations in Hilo.

The assistant recommended Hilo lunch spots: Cafe Pesto (farm-to-table, known for its pesto burger and fresh fish dishes), Hilo Bay Cafe (waterfront dining with Hawaiian, Asian and American flavors), Kuhio Grille (family-owned, classic Hawaiian comfort food), The Fish and The Hog (sustainable seafood) and Miyo's (family-run Japanese cuisine).

The assistant also named Hilo Town Tavern (farm-to-table gastropub), Kalapana Cafe (sandwiches, salads and baked goods) and Punalu'u Bakery (traditional Hawaiian breads and pastries) as lunch or quick-bite options in Hilo.
As of 25 May 2023, the user was thinking of trying local specialties laulau and kalua pig while in Hilo and asked for places that serve traditional Hawaiian dishes.

For laulau the assistant recommended Helena's Hawaiian Food (serving traditional dishes for over 70 years, with pork and beef wrapped in taro leaves and steamed), Kuhio Grille (laulau plate lunch with rice and macaroni salad) and Hilo Bay Cafe (laulau served with poi).

For kalua pig the assistant recommended Cafe Pesto (slow-cooked in an imu, served with cabbage, rice and poi), the Hilo Farmers Market food stalls, and Miyo's (kalua pig plate lunch with rice and macaroni salad).

The assistant described poi (fermented taro root), lomi salmon (salted salmon with diced tomatoes, onions and chili peppers) and haupia (a coconut milk dessert similar to pudding) as traditional Hawaiian dishes to try, and suggested a traditional luau for local specialties.
As of 29 May 2023, the user was looking for a way to display a vintage watch collection, including a favorite 1960s Omega Seamaster, and asked for display case recommendations.
The user recently got a rare blue Snaggletooth action figure from a thrift store a few weeks before 29 May 2023 (roughly early to mid May 2023) and described being on a roll with collectibles lately.

The assistant recommended watch display options: glass-fronted wooden cases (in mahogany, walnut or cherry, with a soft velvety interior), acrylic cases, watch winder cases for automatic watches, shadow box cases and rotating display cases.

The assistant suggested watch display brands WOLF, Orbita, Rapport, The Watch Box Company and Underwood, and advised checking size, material, security (locks or UV-filtering glass) and built-in LED lighting before buying.

As of 29 May 2023, the user liked the idea of a glass-fronted wooden watch case because it sounds elegant and sophisticated, and asked where to find a reputable seller of vintage camera equipment to add a rare camera to the collection.

The assistant suggested camera sources: eBay (look for sellers with feedback above 95%), Etsy, KEH Camera, The Camera Store in Canada, B&H Photo in New York City and the Westlicht Photographica Auction in Vienna.

The assistant suggested camera collector communities such as Reddit's r/VintageCameras and r/CameraCollectors, the Photography-on-the-Net and Fred Miranda forums, and local camera clubs, plus the photography auctions of Christie's and Sotheby's for rare cameras.
As of 29 May 2023, the user was considering starting a collection of first edition novels by favorite authors and asked for online bookstores or resources for finding rare titles.

The assistant recommended rare-book resources: AbeBooks, Biblio, Alibris, eBay, ILAB, the Antiquarian Booksellers Association of America (ABAA), Rare Book Hub, BookFinder (indexing over 150,000 booksellers), The Strand in New York City and Peter Harrington Rare Books in the UK.

As of 29 May 2023, the user had already found a first edition of The Catcher in the Rye by J.D. Salinger and was now looking for a rare Pokémon trading card, specifically the Pikachu Illustrator card, and asked for online marketplaces to find it.

The assistant suggested Pikachu Illustrator sources: eBay (watch for counterfeits), Card Kingdom, TCGplayer, PokéMart, the r/pkmncollectors subreddit, Heritage Auctions and Goldin Auctions, and grading companies PSA and BGS whose graded listings show authenticity and condition.

As of 29 May 2023, the user had collectible coins scattered around the apartment, from over 20 countries including rare coins from ancient Greece and Rome, and spent the weekend before 29 May 2023 sorting them into specialized albums and folders.

The assistant advised storing coins in acid-free albums, individual coin cases or capsules, and coin boxes with dividers, handling coins with clean dry hands or gloves, keeping them out of direct sunlight, and avoiding extreme temperature and humidity.

The assistant suggested displaying coins in glass or acrylic display cases, shadow boxes, coin racks with individual slots, and rotating displays, and recommended having rare or valuable coins graded and certified by PCGS or NGC.

As of 29 May 2023, the user had bought a pair of the limited edition Nike Air Jordan 'Black Toe' sneakers in the user's size from a reputable seller, after checking online marketplaces and sneaker forums daily.
The user's limited edition Nike Air Jordan 'Black Toe' sneakers arrived in the week of 22 May 2023, and the user had been wearing them non-stop since then.

The assistant advised keeping sneakers in their original boxes or dust bags, storing them on shelves or racks, using display cases with individual slots or shadow boxes, and using rotating displays to view the sneakers from different angles.

The assistant also advised cleaning sneakers regularly with a soft-bristled brush and gentle cleaning solution, avoiding direct sunlight and extreme temperature or humidity, and handling them carefully to avoid stretching, bending or creasing the materials.
As of 20 March 2023, the user was trying to attend at least one charity event per month and found the experience incredible, and asked for advice on finding volunteer opportunities in the local area.
The user ran 5 kilometers in the 'Run for Hunger' charity event on 12 March 2023 and raised $250 for a local food bank.

The assistant suggested finding volunteer opportunities through VolunteerMatch, Idealist, the LinkedIn Volunteer Marketplace, local non-profits, social media, community centers, networking, national organizations such as the American Red Cross, Habitat for Humanity and the Sierra Club, local government websites and volunteer fairs.
As of 20 March 2023, the user was interested in fitness-related volunteer opportunities, having recently done charity fitness challenges that helped the user stay motivated.

The assistant suggested fitness volunteering options: charity runs, walks, cycles or swims; teaching free or low-cost fitness classes for seniors, youth or people with disabilities; sports coaching or mentoring; adaptive sports programs such as wheelchair basketball; and volunteering at YMCA or community recreation centers.

The assistant suggested the National Fitness Foundation and the American Council on Exercise as national organizations to check for fitness volunteer roles, and advised reaching out to local fitness studios, gyms and recreation centers about their volunteer programs.

As of 20 March 2023, the user was interested in fitness volunteering, especially charity runs, and was thinking of another charity run soon, maybe a 10K or even a half marathon, and asked for websites to find charity runs nearby.

The assistant listed resources for finding charity runs: Charity Runner, Active.com, RunningUSA, RaceRoster, Charity Navigator, USA Track & Field (USATF), local running stores, local running groups on social media and local charity websites.
As of 20 March 2023, the user was thinking of raising money again for a local food bank through the next charity run.

The assistant advised setting a fundraising goal, creating a page on GoFundMe, Kickstarter or Facebook Fundraisers, sharing the story on social media and by email, getting sponsors per mile, hosting a bake sale, charity yoga class or potluck, and approaching local businesses for sponsorship.
As of 20 March 2023, the user was thinking of setting up a fundraising page on Facebook Fundraisers and asked how to set one up.

The assistant gave a ten-step guide to setting up a Facebook Fundraiser: log in to Facebook, open Fundraisers, click Raise Money, choose a nonprofit such as the local food bank, set a goal, add a title and description, add a photo or video, set a deadline, invite friends and share, and track progress.
As of 20 March 2023, the user planned to set up the Facebook Fundraiser right away and thanked the assistant for the guidance.
As of 20 March 2023, the user had been doing well with exercising regularly and wanted tips for keeping the momentum going.

In the weeks before 20 March 2023, the user volunteered at a charity bake sale that raised $1,000 for the local children's hospital, which the user described as amazing to see how much impact a community can make.

The assistant gave ten tips for staying motivated to exercise: set specific achievable goals, create a routine, find an exercise you enjoy, vary the workouts, track progress, make it social, reward yourself, focus on how you feel, be kind to yourself and celebrate milestones.
As of 20 March 2023, the user wanted to do another charity event, either a run or a cycling event, to stay motivated, and asked for recommendations on finding charity events in the local area.

The assistant suggested finding local charity events through Active.com, Eventbrite, Charity Navigator, social media hashtags and follows, local running or cycling stores, community boards, charity websites, local newspaper listings and asking friends.
As of 20 March 2023, the user was thinking of doing a cycling event, a 10K or 20K ride, had never done a charity cycling event before, and asked for tips on preparing.

For a first charity cycling event, the assistant advised getting a bike check-up, a properly fitting helmet, cycling shoes and padded shorts, starting with 5-10 km rides and building up, riding 2-3 times a week with one 15-20 km weekend ride, and practicing bike handling.

The assistant also advised checking the course map and elevation profile, planning nutrition and hydration, arriving early for registration and bike checks, training with a buddy or cycling group, and taking rest days and stretching.

As of 20 March 2023, the user had fundraising experience, including helping raise over $1,000 for the local children's hospital at a charity bake sale, and asked for tips on fundraising for a charity cycling event.

The assistant recommended fundraising tactics for the cycling event: setting a realistic goal, creating a page on JustGiving, Fundly or Charity Navigator, asking local businesses or cycling clubs for sponsorship, arranging matching gifts, and running mini challenges such as 'Sponsor a mile' or 'Donate $10 for every hill I climb'.
As of 20 March 2023, the user was considering asking the user's employer to match the fundraising goal or make a corporate donation for the cycling event, and asked how to approach the employer.

The assistant advised checking the company's intranet, handbook or website for a corporate social responsibility program or matching gift policy, then preparing a pitch covering the event, the charity's fit with company values, the user's personal connection to the cause and the specific ask.

The assistant advised requesting a meeting with a manager, HR representative or corporate social responsibility officer, being flexible about a partial match or an in-kind donation, following up in writing, and publicly thanking the employer if it agrees to support the fundraising.

The assistant provided a sample email titled 'Request for Corporate Support for Charity Cycling Event' asking the manager for a corporate donation or matching gift for the user's charity cycling event.
As of 20 March 2023, the user was planning to take part in another charity run soon and asked for tips on staying motivated during training.
In February 2023 the user completed a charity fitness challenge and raised $500 for the American Cancer Society, which the user described as a great feeling.

The assistant gave ten training motivation tips: set achievable mini-goals, create a routine, find a running buddy or accountability partner, track progress with an app or log, reward yourself, remember the cause, mix up routes, invest in comfortable gear, focus on how running feels, and celebrate small wins.

As of 20 March 2023, the user was going to try the motivation tips and was thinking of volunteering at a local charity event soon, asking whether any organizations needed help with event planning or execution.

The assistant suggested finding event volunteer roles through local non-profits (using GuideStar or Charity Navigator), volunteer matching platforms such as VolunteerMatch, Idealist and LinkedIn Volunteer Marketplace, social media and event calendars such as Eventbrite and Lanyrd, community centers, places of worship, and friends and family.

The assistant named organizations that may need event help: the American Cancer Society (Relay For Life, Making Strides Against Breast Cancer), the American Heart Association (Heart Walk, Heart Ball), the American Red Cross (blood drives, disaster relief events), local food banks, animal shelters and parks and recreation departments.
As of 20 March 2023, the user planned to check those volunteering resources, was also considering a charity bike ride soon, and asked for tips on preparing for a long bike ride.

The assistant advised starting with 20-30 mile rides and building up gradually, adding interval, strength and hill-repeat training, getting a bike tune-up, checking tire pressure, lubing the chain, and packing a repair kit with spare tubes and a pump or CO2 cartridges.

The assistant also advised visualizing success, setting realistic ride goals, staying hydrated and fueled, dressing in breathable layers, packing snacks, water, sunscreen and a basic first-aid kit, knowing the route, and riding with a buddy or group.
As of 20 March 2023, the user was thinking of asking friends to join the charity bike ride and asked for tips on recruiting them and making it a fun group experience.

The assistant advised recruiting friends through personal invitations, social media shoutouts, a group chat or email thread, and emphasizing the social fun, and suggested a team name and costumes, group training rides, friendly fundraising challenges, a post-ride celebration and a designated team captain.
As of 20 March 2023, the user planned to share charity experiences on social media to inspire others to get involved and asked for tips on sharing the story effectively and making an impact online.

The assistant advised crafting an authentic story with a clear narrative and highlighted impact, and choosing platforms: Facebook for longer updates and fundraisers, Instagram for visual content, Twitter for bite-sized updates and statistics, and blogging or vlogging for in-depth reflections.

The assistant also advised using photos, short videos and infographics, responding to comments, using hashtags, tagging supporters, posting regularly at peak times, scheduling posts with Hootsuite or Buffer, and checking the charity's guidelines before sharing a story online.
